LESSON: PUNCTUATIO N MARKS • HYPHEN • SLASH

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: French Braille Notation
Topic 9.3: Punctuatio n Marks • Hyphen • Slash
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Punctuatio n Marks • Hyphen • Slash, part of French Braille Notation in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do we identify hyphens and slash correctly in French Braille?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. tactile embossed Braille flashcards with individual punctuation marks (hyphen and slash) and common word examples like (vingt-et-un, lundi-vendredi, et/ou, and 25/12) and discuss with peers in class,

2. take turns in reading aloud simple Braille sentences in French braille book using hyphens and slashes in real-life contexts to construct sentences (Le match est prévu pour lundi- vendredi, faut apporter son

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. tactile embossed Braille flashcards with individual punctuation marks (hyphen and slash) and common word examples like (vingt-et-un, lundi-vendredi, et/ou, and 25/12) and discuss with peers in class,
2. take turns in reading aloud simple Braille sentences in French braille book using hyphens and slashes in real-life contexts to construct sentences (Le match est prévu pour lundi- vendredi, faut apporter son

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Punctuatio n Marks • Hyphen • Slash together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: the learner takes turns in reading aloud simple Braille sentences in French braille book using hyphens and slashes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer education: the learner guides each other to write dictated or self-composed French sentences using hyphens and slashes

appropriately.
